inputs.original_text: Workers employed in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth staged a protest outside the Presidential Palace on Thursday and announced a 24-hour strike, calling for legally binding job security guarantees — even as the government argued it had already delivered on the most significant demands. At the heart of the [...]
inputs.modified_text: These essential workers in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth are standing up against systemic exploitation by protesting outside the Presidential Palace on Thursday and launching a 24-hour strike. Their fight for legally binding job security guarantees directly confronts the precarious conditions that have long kept public sector workers vulnerable and marginalized. The government's assertion that they've already met the most significant demands amounts to a clear tactic for upholding the status quo of inequality instead of delivering meaningful institutional reforms. This moment demands we center labor rights and challenge institutions that continue to overlook the needs of working people who sustain our education system.
